## PR Description

Closes #848
### Root Cause

The gh-748 twin-guard cancel path (`cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`) cancelled stale workflow runs while they were still `queued` (pre-materialization). A run's check-suite registers at dispatch time but jobs materialize later — GitHub only concludes a cancelled run's check-runs `cancelled` when jobs exist. A queued cancel therefore orphans the registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with the PAT), seizing mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED (live fa #1457 five ghost cycles, #1520; ghosts #4-#6 on 2026-10-10, after the gh-843 cure side went live).

### Fix

- `js/smAgent.js` — **guard**: before `gh run cancel`, poll `gh api .../actions/runs/<id>` until `status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) within `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs` (default 45s, poll 3s); still queued or probe-degenerate → **defer** the cancel to the next tick. Probe errors also defer — queue waste is always cheaper than a seized gate.
- `js/smAgent.js` — **belt**: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on its head (`checkRunZombies.runIdOf` matching); any still pending is concluded `cancelled` via `PATCH /check-runs/<id>` under the GitHub App token swap (`silentToken` — the PAT gets 403, verified), mirroring `stampValidationChecksForModule`.
- `js/smAgent.js` + `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — **audit**: one marker comment per head per event (`⏸ ghost-guard defer …` / `🧹 ghost-guard clean …`), deduped against existing markers so a head queued across many ticks gets exactly one comment. Bookkeeping-only (gh-755 parity: `cancelled` is never a verdict).
- Supersedes the gh-846 same-tick cancel of *queued* runs — AC3 holds: duplicates are still suppressed, just safely.

### Test Coverage

- RED verified: the 4 new reproduction tests FAIL against the pre-fix code (queued run cancelled immediately, no belt, no audit).
- `test_smAgent.js` — 5 new/rewritten cases: defer on queued (ghost-window replay), cancel after materialization, belt concludes only the cancelled run's pending check-runs (App-token swap asserted), multi-run sweep (queued deferred + in_progress cancelled), audit dedupe per head.
- `test_validationLiveness.js` — 4 marker round-trip/parse/degeneracy cases.
- Full suite: **2504 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Tunables: `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs = 0` restores the legacy cancel-immediately escape hatch.
- Deferral cost: a superseded run may keep occupying the queue until its jobs materialize (one or more ticks) — accepted by design; the gh-842/843 cure-side sweep remains the general ghost backstop.

## Goal

The gh-748 twin-guard must never cancel a workflow run before its jobs have materialized — a cancel in the queued/pre-materialization window orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with a PAT), and the merge gate then holds on dead check-runs indefinitely.

## Subject

js engine twin-guard cancel path (dmtools-agents). Live (fa, 2026-10-10, ghosts #4/#5/#6 AFTER the #843 cure-side fix went live): the tick dispatches validation on a PR head; a duplicate dispatch is cancelled by gh-748 within seconds; the duplicate's check-suite (registered at dispatch time, e.g. 21:40:01 — 12s after the 21:39:48 dispatch) is left `in_progress` with an unresolvable run link; mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED permanently. fa #1457 survived FIVE ghost cycles today (2h+ operator cost); fa #1520 seized the same way; every validated machine PR is at risk. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4

- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T23:53:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #848
### Root Cause

The gh-748 twin-guard cancel path (`cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`) cancelled stale workflow runs while they were still `queued` (pre-materialization). A run's check-suite registers at dispatch time but jobs materialize later — GitHub only concludes a cancelled run's check-runs `cancelled` when jobs exist. A queued cancel therefore orphans the registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with the PAT), seizing mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED (live fa #1457 five ghost cycles, #1520; ghosts #4-#6 on 2026-10-10, after the gh-843 cure side went live).

### Fix

- `js/smAgent.js` — **guard**: before `gh run cancel`, poll `gh api .../actions/runs/<id>` until `status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) within `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs` (default 45s, poll 3s); still queued or probe-degenerate → **defer** the cancel to the next tick. Probe errors also defer — queue waste is always cheaper than a seized gate.
- `js/smAgent.js` — **belt**: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on its head (`checkRunZombies.runIdOf` matching); any still pending is concluded `cancelled` via `PATCH /check-runs/<id>` under the GitHub App token swap (`silentToken` — the PAT gets 403, verified), mirroring `stampValidationChecksForModule`.
- `js/smAgent.js` + `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — **audit**: one marker comment per head per event (`⏸ ghost-guard defer …` / `🧹 ghost-guard clean …`), deduped against existing markers so a head queued across many ticks gets exactly one comment. Bookkeeping-only (gh-755 parity: `cancelled` is never a verdict).
- Supersedes the gh-846 same-tick cancel of *queued* runs — AC3 holds: duplicates are still suppressed, just safely.

### Test Coverage

- RED verified: the 4 new reproduction tests FAIL against the pre-fix code (queued run cancelled immediately, no belt, no audit).
- `test_smAgent.js` — 5 new/rewritten cases: defer on queued (ghost-window replay), cancel after materialization, belt concludes only the cancelled run's pending check-runs (App-token swap asserted), multi-run sweep (queued deferred + in_progress cancelled), audit dedupe per head.
- `test_validationLiveness.js` — 4 marker round-trip/parse/degeneracy cases.
- Full suite: **2504 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Tunables: `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs = 0` restores the legacy cancel-immediately escape hatch.
- Deferral cost: a superseded run may keep occupying the queue until its jobs materialize (one or more ticks) — accepted by design; the gh-842/843 cure-side sweep remains the general ghost backstop.

## Description

## Goal

The gh-748 twin-guard must never cancel a workflow run before its jobs have materialized — a cancel in the queued/pre-materialization window orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with a PAT), and the merge gate then holds on dead check-runs indefinitely.

## Subject

js engine twin-guard cancel path (dmtools-agents). Live (fa, 2026-10-10, ghosts #4/#5/#6 AFTER the #843 cure-side fix went live): the tick dispatches validation on a PR head; a duplicate dispatch is cancelled by gh-748 within seconds; the duplicate's check-suite (registered at dispatch time, e.g. 21:40:01 — 12s after the 21:39:48 dispatch) is left `in_progress` with an unresolvable run link; mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED permanently. fa #1457 survived FIVE ghost cycles today (2h+ operator cost); fa #1520 seized the same way; every validated machine PR is at risk. Evidence chain: gh-842 comment thread (ghost #1..#6 timelines, check-run dumps, minter correction — the twin is a duplicate DISPATCH, fa CI is already dispatch-only).

## Capability surface

- Guard: before `gh run cancel`, poll the target until `run.status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) with a short timeout; if still queued, DEFER the cancel to the next tick instead of cancelling (a live-materialized cancel marks check-runs `cancelled`, which is a clean terminal state).
- Belt: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on the head; any still `in_progress`/`queued` gets concluded via the Checks API (requires the GitHub App token — PAT gets 403, verified) or a re-dispatch of a single-leg workflow that re-stamps the contexts.
- Audit: one marker comment per head noting the deferred/cleaned cancel.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay ghost #5's exact timeline (dispatch 21:39:48, ghost 21:40:01) — no orphaned in_progress check-run remains on the head.
2. AC2: zero ghost-signature check-runs (in_progress + unresolvable run link) across a 24h soak on fa.
3. AC3: the twin-guard still prevents parallel validation waste (duplicate dispatches are still suppressed, just safely).
4. AC4: fa #1457-class PRs merge without operator resets once the fa pin carries the fix.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests — cancel deferred on queued; check-run cleanup after materialized cancel.
- L2: replay the real 21:39-21:41 timeline from fa check-run dumps (in gh-842).
- L3 (live): soak metric — ghost count on fa = 0/day.

## Non-goals

- The gh-843 cure side (detect/refresh/re-dispatch) — already shipped.
- Changing the dispatch-only CI topology — already in place on fa.

- gh-842 (full evidence archive, ghosts #1-#6).
- fa #1457 (five ghost cycles), fa #1520 (ghost #6).
- gh-755 (cancelled is never a verdict), gh-748 (twin-guard family).

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-848` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +584
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T23:53:21Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T23:53:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #848
### Root Cause

The gh-748 twin-guard cancel path (`cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`) cancelled stale workflow runs while they were still `queued` (pre-materialization). A run's check-suite registers at dispatch time but jobs materialize later — GitHub only concludes a cancelled run's check-runs `cancelled` when jobs exist. A queued cancel therefore orphans the registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with the PAT), seizing mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED (live fa #1457 five ghost cycles, #1520; ghosts #4-#6 on 2026-10-10, after the gh-843 cure side went live).

### Fix

- `js/smAgent.js` — **guard**: before `gh run cancel`, poll `gh api .../actions/runs/<id>` until `status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) within `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs` (default 45s, poll 3s); still queued or probe-degenerate → **defer** the cancel to the next tick. Probe errors also defer — queue waste is always cheaper than a seized gate.
- `js/smAgent.js` — **belt**: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on its head (`checkRunZombies.runIdOf` matching); any still pending is concluded `cancelled` via `PATCH /check-runs/<id>` under the GitHub App token swap (`silentToken` — the PAT gets 403, verified), mirroring `stampValidationChecksForModule`.
- `js/smAgent.js` + `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — **audit**: one marker comment per head per event (`⏸ ghost-guard defer …` / `🧹 ghost-guard clean …`), deduped against existing markers so a head queued across many ticks gets exactly one comment. Bookkeeping-only (gh-755 parity: `cancelled` is never a verdict).
- Supersedes the gh-846 same-tick cancel of *queued* runs — AC3 holds: duplicates are still suppressed, just safely.

### Test Coverage

- RED verified: the 4 new reproduction tests FAIL against the pre-fix code (queued run cancelled immediately, no belt, no audit).
- `test_smAgent.js` — 5 new/rewritten cases: defer on queued (ghost-window replay), cancel after materialization, belt concludes only the cancelled run's pending check-runs (App-token swap asserted), multi-run sweep (queued deferred + in_progress cancelled), audit dedupe per head.
- `test_validationLiveness.js` — 4 marker round-trip/parse/degeneracy cases.
- Full suite: **2504 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Tunables: `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs = 0` restores the legacy cancel-immediately escape hatch.
- Deferral cost: a superseded run may keep occupying the queue until its jobs materialize (one or more ticks) — accepted by design; the gh-842/843 cure-side sweep remains the general ghost backstop.

## Goal

The gh-748 twin-guard must never cancel a workflow run before its jobs have materialized — a cancel in the queued/pre-materialization window orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with a PAT), and the merge gate then holds on dead check-runs indefinitely.

## Subject

js engine twin-guard cancel path (dmtools-agents). Live (fa, 2026-10-10, ghosts #4/#5/#6 AFTER the #843 cure-side fix went live): the tick dispatches validation on a PR head; a duplicate dispatch is cancelled by gh-748 within seconds; the duplicate's check-suite (registered at dispatch time, e.g. 21:40:01 — 12s after the 21:39:48 dispatch) is left `in_progress` with an unresolvable run link; mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED permanently. fa #1457 survived FIVE ghost cycles today (2h+ operator cost); fa #1520 seized the same way; every validated machine PR is at risk. Evidence chain: gh-842 comment thread (ghost #1..#6 timelines, check-run dumps, minter correction — the twin is a duplicate DISPATCH, fa CI is already dispatch-only).

## Capability surface

- Guard: before `gh run cancel`, poll the target until `run.status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) with a short timeout; if still queued, DEFER the cancel to the next tick instead of cancelling (a live-materialized cancel marks check-runs `cancelled`, which is a clean terminal state).
- Belt: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on the head; any still `in_progress`/`queued` gets concluded via the Checks API (requires the GitHub App token — PAT gets 403, verified) or a re-dispatch of a single-leg workflow that re-stamps the contexts.
- Audit: one marker comment per head noting the deferred/cleaned cancel.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay ghost #5's exact timeline (dispatch 21:39:48, ghost 21:40:01) — no orphaned in_progress check-run remains on the head.
2. AC2: zero ghost-signature check-runs (in_progress + unresolvable run link) across a 24h soak on fa.
3. AC3: the twin-guard still prevents parallel validation waste (duplicate dispatches are still suppressed, just safely).
4. AC4: fa #1457-class PRs merge without operator resets once the fa pin carries the fix.

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T23:53:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #848
### Root Cause

The gh-748 twin-guard cancel path (`cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`) cancelled stale workflow runs while they were still `queued` (pre-materialization). A run's check-suite registers at dispatch time but jobs materialize later — GitHub only concludes a cancelled run's check-runs `cancelled` when jobs exist. A queued cancel therefore orphans the registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with the PAT), seizing mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED (live fa #1457 five ghost cycles, #1520; ghosts #4-#6 on 2026-10-10, after the gh-843 cure side went live).

### Fix

- `js/smAgent.js` — **guard**: before `gh run cancel`, poll `gh api .../actions/runs/<id>` until `status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) within `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs` (default 45s, poll 3s); still queued or probe-degenerate → **defer** the cancel to the next tick. Probe errors also defer — queue waste is always cheaper than a seized gate.
- `js/smAgent.js` — **belt**: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on its head (`checkRunZombies.runIdOf` matching); any still pending is concluded `cancelled` via `PATCH /check-runs/<id>` under the GitHub App token swap (`silentToken` — the PAT gets 403, verified), mirroring `stampValidationChecksForModule`.
- `js/smAgent.js` + `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — **audit**: one marker comment per head per event (`⏸ ghost-guard defer …` / `🧹 ghost-guard clean …`), deduped against existing markers so a head queued across many ticks gets exactly one comment. Bookkeeping-only (gh-755 parity: `cancelled` is never a verdict).
- Supersedes the gh-846 same-tick cancel of *queued* runs — AC3 holds: duplicates are still suppressed, just safely.

### Test Coverage

- RED verified: the 4 new reproduction tests FAIL against the pre-fix code (queued run cancelled immediately, no belt, no audit).
- `test_smAgent.js` — 5 new/rewritten cases: defer on queued (ghost-window replay), cancel after materialization, belt concludes only the cancelled run's pending check-runs (App-token swap asserted), multi-run sweep (queued deferred + in_progress cancelled), audit dedupe per head.
- `test_validationLiveness.js` — 4 marker round-trip/parse/degeneracy cases.
- Full suite: **2504 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Tunables: `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs = 0` restores the legacy cancel-immediately escape hatch.
- Deferral cost: a superseded run may keep occupying the queue until its jobs materialize (one or more ticks) — accepted by design; the gh-842/843 cure-side sweep remains the general ghost backstop.

## Description

## Goal

The gh-748 twin-guard must never cancel a workflow run before its jobs have materialized — a cancel in the queued/pre-materialization window orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with a PAT), and the merge gate then holds on dead check-runs indefinitely.

## Subject

js engine twin-guard cancel path (dmtools-agents). Live (fa, 2026-10-10, ghosts #4/#5/#6 AFTER the #843 cure-side fix went live): the tick dispatches validation on a PR head; a duplicate dispatch is cancelled by gh-748 within seconds; the duplicate's check-suite (registered at dispatch time, e.g. 21:40:01 — 12s after the 21:39:48 dispatch) is left `in_progress` with an unresolvable run link; mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED permanently. fa #1457 survived FIVE ghost cycles today (2h+ operator cost); fa #1520 seized the same way; every validated machine PR is at risk. Evidence chain: gh-842 comment thread (ghost #1..#6 timelines, check-run dumps, minter correction — the twin is a duplicate DISPATCH, fa CI is already dispatch-only).

## Capability surface

- Guard: before `gh run cancel`, poll the target until `run.status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) with a short timeout; if still queued, DEFER the cancel to the next tick instead of cancelling (a live-materialized cancel marks check-runs `cancelled`, which is a clean terminal state).
- Belt: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on the head; any still `in_progress`/`queued` gets concluded via the Checks API (requires the GitHub App token — PAT gets 403, verified) or a re-dispatch of a single-leg workflow that re-stamps the contexts.
- Audit: one marker comment per head noting the deferred/cleaned cancel.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay ghost #5's exact timeline (dispatch 21:39:48, ghost 21:40:01) — no orphaned in_progress check-run remains on the head.
2. AC2: zero ghost-signature check-runs (in_progress + unresolvable run link) across a 24h soak on fa.
3. AC3: the twin-guard still prevents parallel validation waste (duplicate dispatches are still suppressed, just safely).
4. AC4: fa #1457-class PRs merge without operator resets once the fa pin carries the fix.

- L1: unit tests — cancel deferred on queued; check-run cleanup after materialized cancel.
- L2: replay the real 21:39-21:41 timeline from fa check-run dumps (in gh-842).
- L3 (live): soak metric — ghost count on fa = 0/day.

## Non-goals

- The gh-843 cure side (detect/refresh/re-dispatch) — already shipped.
- Changing the dispatch-only CI topology — already in place on fa.

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-848` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4

- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T23:53:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #848
### Root Cause

The gh-748 twin-guard cancel path (`cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`) cancelled stale workflow runs while they were still `queued` (pre-materialization). A run's check-suite registers at dispatch time but jobs materialize later — GitHub only concludes a cancelled run's check-runs `cancelled` when jobs exist. A queued cancel therefore orphans the registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with the PAT), seizing mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED (live fa #1457 five ghost cycles, #1520; ghosts #4-#6 on 2026-10-10, after the gh-843 cure side went live).

### Fix

- `js/smAgent.js` — **guard**: before `gh run cancel`, poll `gh api .../actions/runs/<id>` until `status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) within `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs` (default 45s, poll 3s); still queued or probe-degenerate → **defer** the cancel to the next tick. Probe errors also defer — queue waste is always cheaper than a seized gate.
- `js/smAgent.js` — **belt**: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on its head (`checkRunZombies.runIdOf` matching); any still pending is concluded `cancelled` via `PATCH /check-runs/<id>` under the GitHub App token swap (`silentToken` — the PAT gets 403, verified), mirroring `stampValidationChecksForModule`.
- `js/smAgent.js` + `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — **audit**: one marker comment per head per event (`⏸ ghost-guard defer …` / `🧹 ghost-guard clean …`), deduped against existing markers so a head queued across many ticks gets exactly one comment. Bookkeeping-only (gh-755 parity: `cancelled` is never a verdict).
- Supersedes the gh-846 same-tick cancel of *queued* runs — AC3 holds: duplicates are still suppressed, just safely.

### Test Coverage

- RED verified: the 4 new reproduction tests FAIL against the pre-fix code (queued run cancelled immediately, no belt, no audit).
- `test_smAgent.js` — 5 new/rewritten cases: defer on queued (ghost-window replay), cancel after materialization, belt concludes only the cancelled run's pending check-runs (App-token swap asserted), multi-run sweep (queued deferred + in_progress cancelled), audit dedupe per head.
- `test_validationLiveness.js` — 4 marker round-trip/parse/degeneracy cases.
- Full suite: **2504 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Tunables: `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs = 0` restores the legacy cancel-immediately escape hatch.
- Deferral cost: a superseded run may keep occupying the queue until its jobs materialize (one or more ticks) — accepted by design; the gh-842/843 cure-side sweep remains the general ghost backstop.

# gh-848: [GOAL] MINTER fix: gh-748 cancels runs pre-materialization → orphaned in_progress check-runs seize the merge gate (ghosts #4-#6 on fa TODAY, after #843 cure went live)

## Description

## Goal

The gh-748 twin-guard must never cancel a workflow run before its jobs have materialized — a cancel in the queued/pre-materialization window orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with a PAT), and the merge gate then holds on dead check-runs indefinitely.

## Subject

js engine twin-guard cancel path (dmtools-agents). Live (fa, 2026-10-10, ghosts #4/#5/#6 AFTER the #843 cure-side fix went live): the tick dispatches validation on a PR head; a duplicate dispatch is cancelled by gh-748 within seconds; the duplicate's check-suite (registered at dispatch time, e.g. 21:40:01 — 12s after the 21:39:48 dispatch) is left `in_progress` with an unresolvable run link; mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED permanently. fa #1457 survived FIVE ghost cycles today (2h+ operator cost); fa #1520 seized the same way; every validated machine PR is at risk. Evidence chain: gh-842 comment thread (ghost #1..#6 timelines, check-run dumps, minter correction — the twin is a duplicate DISPATCH, fa CI is already dispatch-only).

## Capability surface

- Guard: before `gh run cancel`, poll the target until `run.status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) with a short timeout; if still queued, DEFER the cancel to the next tick instead of cancelling (a live-materialized cancel marks check-runs `cancelled`, which is a clean terminal state).
- Belt: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on the head; any still `in_progress`/`queued` gets concluded via the Checks API (requires the GitHub App token — PAT gets 403, verified) or a re-dispatch of a single-leg workflow that re-stamps the contexts.
- Audit: one marker comment per head noting the deferred/cleaned cancel.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay ghost #5's exact timeline (dispatch 21:39:48, ghost 21:40:01) — no orphaned in_progress check-run remains on the head.
2. AC2: zero ghost-signature check-runs (in_progress + unresolvable run link) across a 24h soak on fa.
3. AC3: the twin-guard still prevents parallel validation waste (duplicate dispatches are still suppressed, just safely).
4. AC4: fa #1457-class PRs merge without operator resets once the fa pin carries the fix.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests — cancel deferred on queued; check-run cleanup after materialized cancel.
- L2: replay the real 21:39-21:41 timeline from fa check-run dumps (in gh-842).

## PR Description

Closes #848
### Root Cause

The gh-748 twin-guard cancel path (`cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`) cancelled stale workflow runs while they were still `queued` (pre-materialization). A run's check-suite registers at dispatch time but jobs materialize later — GitHub only concludes a cancelled run's check-runs `cancelled` when jobs exist. A queued cancel therefore orphans the registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with the PAT), seizing mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED (live fa #1457 five ghost cycles, #1520; ghosts #4-#6 on 2026-10-10, after the gh-843 cure side went live).

### Fix

- `js/smAgent.js` — **guard**: before `gh run cancel`, poll `gh api .../actions/runs/<id>` until `status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) within `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs` (default 45s, poll 3s); still queued or probe-degenerate → **defer** the cancel to the next tick. Probe errors also defer — queue waste is always cheaper than a seized gate.
- `js/smAgent.js` — **belt**: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on its head (`checkRunZombies.runIdOf` matching); any still pending is concluded `cancelled` via `PATCH /check-runs/<id>` under the GitHub App token swap (`silentToken` — the PAT gets 403, verified), mirroring `stampValidationChecksForModule`.
- `js/smAgent.js` + `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — **audit**: one marker comment per head per event (`⏸ ghost-guard defer …` / `🧹 ghost-guard clean …`), deduped against existing markers so a head queued across many ticks gets exactly one comment. Bookkeeping-only (gh-755 parity: `cancelled` is never a verdict).
- Supersedes the gh-846 same-tick cancel of *queued* runs — AC3 holds: duplicates are still suppressed, just safely.

### Test Coverage

- RED verified: the 4 new reproduction tests FAIL against the pre-fix code (queued run cancelled immediately, no belt, no audit).
- `test_smAgent.js` — 5 new/rewritten cases: defer on queued (ghost-window replay), cancel after materialization, belt concludes only the cancelled run's pending check-runs (App-token swap asserted), multi-run sweep (queued deferred + in_progress cancelled), audit dedupe per head.
- `test_validationLiveness.js` — 4 marker round-trip/parse/degeneracy cases.
- Full suite: **2504 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Tunables: `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs = 0` restores the legacy cancel-immediately escape hatch.
- Deferral cost: a superseded run may keep occupying the queue until its jobs materialize (one or more ticks) — accepted by design; the gh-842/843 cure-side sweep remains the general ghost backstop.

## Description

## Goal

The gh-748 twin-guard must never cancel a workflow run before its jobs have materialized — a cancel in the queued/pre-materialization window orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with a PAT), and the merge gate then holds on dead check-runs indefinitely.

## Subject

js engine twin-guard cancel path (dmtools-agents). Live (fa, 2026-10-10, ghosts #4/#5/#6 AFTER the #843 cure-side fix went live): the tick dispatches validation on a PR head; a duplicate dispatch is cancelled by gh-748 within seconds; the duplicate's check-suite (registered at dispatch time, e.g. 21:40:01 — 12s after the 21:39:48 dispatch) is left `in_progress` with an unresolvable run link; mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED permanently. fa #1457 survived FIVE ghost cycles today (2h+ operator cost); fa #1520 seized the same way; every validated machine PR is at risk. Evidence chain: gh-842 comment thread (ghost #1..#6 timelines, check-run dumps, minter correction — the twin is a duplicate DISPATCH, fa CI is already dispatch-only).

## Capability surface

- Guard: before `gh run cancel`, poll the target until `run.status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) with a short timeout; if still queued, DEFER the cancel to the next tick instead of cancelling (a live-materialized cancel marks check-runs `cancelled`, which is a clean terminal state).

- Audit: one marker comment per head noting the deferred/cleaned cancel.

- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T23:53:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #848
### Root Cause

The gh-748 twin-guard cancel path (`cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`) cancelled stale workflow runs while they were still `queued` (pre-materialization). A run's check-suite registers at dispatch time but jobs materialize later — GitHub only concludes a cancelled run's check-runs `cancelled` when jobs exist. A queued cancel therefore orphans the registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with the PAT), seizing mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED (live fa #1457 five ghost cycles, #1520; ghosts #4-#6 on 2026-10-10, after the gh-843 cure side went live).

### Fix

- `js/smAgent.js` — **guard**: before `gh run cancel`, poll `gh api .../actions/runs/<id>` until `status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) within `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs` (default 45s, poll 3s); still queued or probe-degenerate → **defer** the cancel to the next tick. Probe errors also defer — queue waste is always cheaper than a seized gate.
- `js/smAgent.js` — **belt**: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on its head (`checkRunZombies.runIdOf` matching); any still pending is concluded `cancelled` via `PATCH /check-runs/<id>` under the GitHub App token swap (`silentToken` — the PAT gets 403, verified), mirroring `stampValidationChecksForModule`.
- `js/smAgent.js` + `js/common/validationLiveness.js` — **audit**: one marker comment per head per event (`⏸ ghost-guard defer …` / `🧹 ghost-guard clean …`), deduped against existing markers so a head queued across many ticks gets exactly one comment. Bookkeeping-only (gh-755 parity: `cancelled` is never a verdict).
- Supersedes the gh-846 same-tick cancel of *queued* runs — AC3 holds: duplicates are still suppressed, just safely.

### Test Coverage

- RED verified: the 4 new reproduction tests FAIL against the pre-fix code (queued run cancelled immediately, no belt, no audit).
- `test_smAgent.js` — 5 new/rewritten cases: defer on queued (ghost-window replay), cancel after materialization, belt concludes only the cancelled run's pending check-runs (App-token swap asserted), multi-run sweep (queued deferred + in_progress cancelled), audit dedupe per head.
- `test_validationLiveness.js` — 4 marker round-trip/parse/degeneracy cases.
- Full suite: **2504 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Tunables: `jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs = 0` restores the legacy cancel-immediately escape hatch.
- Deferral cost: a superseded run may keep occupying the queue until its jobs materialize (one or more ticks) — accepted by design; the gh-842/843 cure-side sweep remains the general ghost backstop.

## Description

## Goal

The gh-748 twin-guard must never cancel a workflow run before its jobs have materialized — a cancel in the queued/pre-materialization window orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with a PAT), and the merge gate then holds on dead check-runs indefinitely.

## Subject

js engine twin-guard cancel path (dmtools-agents). Live (fa, 2026-10-10, ghosts #4/#5/#6 AFTER the #843 cure-side fix went live): the tick dispatches validation on a PR head; a duplicate dispatch is cancelled by gh-748 within seconds; the duplicate's check-suite (registered at dispatch time, e.g. 21:40:01 — 12s after the 21:39:48 dispatch) is left `in_progress` with an unresolvable run link; mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED permanently. fa #1457 survived FIVE ghost cycles today (2h+ operator cost); fa #1520 seized the same way; every validated machine PR is at risk. Evidence chain: gh-842 comment thread (ghost #1..#6 timelines, check-run dumps, minter correction — the twin is a duplicate DISPATCH, fa CI is already dispatch-only).

## Capability surface

- Guard: before `gh run cancel`, poll the target until `run.status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) with a short timeout; if still queued, DEFER the cancel to the next tick instead of cancelling (a live-materialized cancel marks check-runs `cancelled`, which is a clean terminal state).
- Belt: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on the head; any still `in_progress`/`queued` gets concluded via the Checks API (requires the GitHub App token — PAT gets 403, verified) or a re-dispatch of a single-leg workflow that re-stamps the contexts.
- Audit: one marker comment per head noting the deferred/cleaned cancel.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay ghost #5's exact timeline (dispatch 21:39:48, ghost 21:40:01) — no orphaned in_progress check-run remains on the head.
2. AC2: zero ghost-signature check-runs (in_progress + unresolvable run link) across a 24h soak on fa.
3. AC3: the twin-guard still prevents parallel validation waste (duplicate dispatches are still suppressed, just safely).
4. AC4: fa #1457-class PRs merge without operator resets once the fa pin carries the fix.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests — cancel deferred on queued; check-run cleanup after materialized cancel.
- L2: replay the real 21:39-21:41 timeline from fa check-run dumps (in gh-842).
- L3 (live): soak metric — ghost count on fa = 0/day.

## Non-goals

- The gh-843 cure side (detect/refresh/re-dispatch) — already shipped.
- Changing the dispatch-only CI topology — already in place on fa.

# gh-848: [GOAL] MINTER fix: gh-748 cancels runs pre-materialization → orphaned in_progress check-runs seize the merge gate (ghosts #4-#6 on fa TODAY, after #843 cure went live)

## Description

## Goal

The gh-748 twin-guard must never cancel a workflow run before its jobs have materialized — a cancel in the queued/pre-materialization window orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with a PAT), and the merge gate then holds on dead check-runs indefinitely.

## Subject

js engine twin-guard cancel path (dmtools-agents). Live (fa, 2026-10-10, ghosts #4/#5/#6 AFTER the #843 cure-side fix went live): the tick dispatches validation on a PR head; a duplicate dispatch is cancelled by gh-748 within seconds; the duplicate's check-suite (registered at dispatch time, e.g. 21:40:01 — 12s after the 21:39:48 dispatch) is left `in_progress` with an unresolvable run link; mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED permanently. fa #1457 survived FIVE ghost cycles today (2h+ operator cost); fa #1520 seized the same way; every validated machine PR is at risk. Evidence chain: gh-842 comment thread (ghost #1..#6 timelines, check-run dumps, minter correction — the twin is a duplicate DISPATCH, fa CI is already dispatch-only).

## Capability surface

- Guard: before `gh run cancel`, poll the target until `run.status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) with a short timeout; if still queued, DEFER the cancel to the next tick instead of cancelling (a live-materialized cancel marks check-runs `cancelled`, which is a clean terminal state).
- Belt: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on the head; any still `in_progress`/`queued` gets concluded via the Checks API (requires the GitHub App token — PAT gets 403, verified) or a re-dispatch of a single-leg workflow that re-stamps the contexts.
- Audit: one marker comment per head noting the deferred/cleaned cancel.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay ghost #5's exact timeline (dispatch 21:39:48, ghost 21:40:01) — no orphaned in_progress check-run remains on the head.
2. AC2: zero ghost-signature check-runs (in_progress + unresolvable run link) across a 24h soak on fa.
3. AC3: the twin-guard still prevents parallel validation waste (duplicate dispatches are still suppressed, just safely).
4. AC4: fa #1457-class PRs merge without operator resets once the fa pin carries the fix.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests — cancel deferred on queued; check-run cleanup after materialized cancel.
- L2: replay the real 21:39-21:41 timeline from fa check-run dumps (in gh-842).
- L3 (live): soak metric — ghost count on fa = 0/day.

## Non-goals

- The gh-843 cure side (detect/refresh/re-dispatch) — already shipped.
- Changing the dispatch-only CI topology — already in place on fa.

## References

- gh-842 (full evidence archive, ghosts #1-#6).
- fa #1457 (five ghost cycles), fa #1520 (ghost #6).
- gh-755 (cancelled is never a verdict), gh-748 (twin-guard family).

# gh-848: [GOAL] MINTER fix: gh-748 cancels runs pre-materialization → orphaned in_progress check-runs seize the merge gate (ghosts #4-#6 on fa TODAY, after #843 cure went live)

## Description

## Goal

The gh-748 twin-guard must never cancel a workflow run before its jobs have materialized — a cancel in the queued/pre-materialization window orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with a PAT), and the merge gate then holds on dead check-runs indefinitely.

## Subject

js engine twin-guard cancel path (dmtools-agents). Live (fa, 2026-10-10, ghosts #4/#5/#6 AFTER the #843 cure-side fix went live): the tick dispatches validation on a PR head; a duplicate dispatch is cancelled by gh-748 within seconds; the duplicate's check-suite (registered at dispatch time, e.g. 21:40:01 — 12s after the 21:39:48 dispatch) is left `in_progress` with an unresolvable run link; mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED permanently. fa #1457 survived FIVE ghost cycles today (2h+ operator cost); fa #1520 seized the same way; every validated machine PR is at risk. Evidence chain: gh-842 comment thread (ghost #1..#6 timelines, check-run dumps, minter correction — the twin is a duplicate DISPATCH, fa CI is already dispatch-only).

## Capability surface

- Guard: before `gh run cancel`, poll the target until `run.status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) with a short timeout; if still queued, DEFER the cancel to the next tick instead of cancelling (a live-materialized cancel marks check-runs `cancelled`, which is a clean terminal state).
- Belt: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on the head; any still `in_progress`/`queued` gets concluded via the Checks API (requires the GitHub App token — PAT gets 403, verified) or a re-dispatch of a single-leg workflow that re-stamps the contexts.
- Audit: one marker comment per head noting the deferred/cleaned cancel.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay ghost #5's exact timeline (dispatch 21:39:48, ghost 21:40:01) — no orphaned in_progress check-run remains on the head.
2. AC2: zero ghost-signature check-runs (in_progress + unresolvable run link) across a 24h soak on fa.
3. AC3: the twin-guard still prevents parallel validation waste (duplicate dispatches are still suppressed, just safely).
4. AC4: fa #1457-class PRs merge without operator resets once the fa pin carries the fix.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests — cancel deferred on queued; check-run cleanup after materialized cancel.
- L2: replay the real 21:39-21:41 timeline from fa check-run dumps (in gh-842).
- L3 (live): soak metric — ghost count on fa = 0/day.

## Non-goals

- The gh-843 cure side (detect/refresh/re-dispatch) — already shipped.
- Changing the dispatch-only CI topology — already in place on fa.

## References

- gh-842 (full evidence archive, ghosts #1-#6).
- fa #1457 (five ghost cycles), fa #1520 (ghost #6).
- gh-755 (cancelled is never a verdict), gh-748 (twin-guard family).

Now key review points for the new code:

1. **`sleepMilliseconds` busy-wait fallback**: in the node test harness, busy-wait; in GraalJS bridge, Java sleep. In the SM tick environment (GraalJS), Java.type sleep works. OK. But there's a concern: a 45s blocking poll inside the tick loop for each stale run — could blow tick budget. But the design is documented and accepted.

2. **`waitForRunMaterialized` loop**: `while(true)` — polls, checks `Date.now() >= deadline` AFTER the status check, so the final poll happens at deadline boundary. Fine. Poll interval 3s default; if pollMs=0 and timeoutMs>0, busy spin? sleepMilliseconds(0) returns immediately — infinite tight loop until deadline. Actually with pollMs=0 the loop becomes a tight gh api call loop (each iteration makes an API call) until deadline — 45s of hammering the API. Minor edge case; pollMs=0 not realistic default but tunable. SUGGESTION.

3. **mcpParse of probe**: `mcpParse((res || {}).output || (res || {}).stdout || res)` — need to check mcpParse handles a string vs object. Let me check mcpParse usage.

4. **Deferral per tick**: a run sitting queued for long would be deferred every tick and each defer posts... no — deduped per head via markers. OK.

5. **`concludeOrphanedCheckRuns`**: uses `headCheckRunsSafe` — returns `[]` on empty, `null` on probe failure. Code checks `if (!checkRuns || !checkRuns.length) return 0;` — null degrades to skip. Good. `runIdOf(cr) !== String(cancelledRun.id)` — check runIdOf implementation.

6. **Token swap + `gh api`**: `gh api` uses GH_TOKEN env var. But wait — the cancel command earlier (`gh api -X POST .../cancel`) runs WITHOUT the swap — fine, PAT cancel.

7. **PATCH check-runs `-f status=completed -f conclusion=cancelled`**: fine.

8. **postGhostGuardAudit**: reads comments, dedupes, posts one comment containing all fresh lines. `seen['d:'+sha]` dedupes within call. Marker regex requires `([0-9a-f]{7,40})` sha — head_sha is 40 chars. OK. But note: ghostGuardMarks keyed by full sha; defer marker writes full sha. OK.

# gh-848: [GOAL] MINTER fix: gh-748 cancels runs pre-materialization → orphaned in_progress check-runs seize the merge gate (ghosts #4-#6 on fa TODAY, after #843 cure went live)

## Description

## Goal

The gh-748 twin-guard must never cancel a workflow run before its jobs have materialized — a cancel in the queued/pre-materialization window orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts forever (no run to re-run, no API to conclude them with a PAT), and the merge gate then holds on dead check-runs indefinitely.

## Subject

js engine twin-guard cancel path (dmtools-agents). Live (fa, 2026-10-10, ghosts #4/#5/#6 AFTER the #843 cure-side fix went live): the tick dispatches validation on a PR head; a duplicate dispatch is cancelled by gh-748 within seconds; the duplicate's check-suite (registered at dispatch time, e.g. 21:40:01 — 12s after the 21:39:48 dispatch) is left `in_progress` with an unresolvable run link; mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED permanently. fa #1457 survived FIVE ghost cycles today (2h+ operator cost); fa #1520 seized the same way; every validated machine PR is at risk. Evidence chain: gh-842 comment thread (ghost #1..#6 timelines, check-run dumps, minter correction — the twin is a duplicate DISPATCH, fa CI is already dispatch-only).

## Capability surface

- Guard: before `gh run cancel`, poll the target until `run.status != 'queued'` (jobs materialized) with a short timeout; if still queued, DEFER the cancel to the next tick instead of cancelling (a live-materialized cancel marks check-runs `cancelled`, which is a clean terminal state).
- Belt: after ANY cancel, list the cancelled run's check-runs on the head; any still `in_progress`/`queued` gets concluded via the Checks API (requires the GitHub App token — PAT gets 403, verified) or a re-dispatch of a single-leg workflow that re-stamps the contexts.
- Audit: one marker comment per head noting the deferred/cleaned cancel.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay ghost #5's exact timeline (dispatch 21:39:48, ghost 21:40:01) — no orphaned in_progress check-run remains on the head.
2. AC2: zero ghost-signature check-runs (in_progress + unresolvable run link) across a 24h soak on fa.
3. AC3: the twin-guard still prevents parallel validation waste (duplicate dispatches are still suppressed, just safely).
4. AC4: fa #1457-class PRs merge without operator resets once the fa pin carries the fix.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests — cancel deferred on queued; check-run cleanup after materialized cancel.
- L2: replay the real 21:39-21:41 timeline from fa check-run dumps (in gh-842).
- L3 (live): soak metric — ghost count on fa = 0/day.

## Non-goals

- The gh-843 cure side (detect/refresh/re-dispatch) — already shipped.
- Changing the dispatch-only CI topology — already in place on fa.

## References

- gh-842 (full evidence archive, ghosts #1-#6).
- fa #1457 (five ghost cycles), fa #1520 (ghost #6).
- gh-755 (cancelled is never a verdict), gh-748 (twin-guard family).

**Analysis of the core logic:**

1. **Guard deferral + polling in tick loop** — blocking `waitForRunMaterialized` up to 45s per stale run inside `cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`, which runs inside `processRule`. With multiple stale runs, tick time extends significantly. Documented and accepted (PR notes). SUGGESTION at most.

2. **`waitForRunMaterialized` pollMs=0 edge** — `cancelMaterializePollMs: 0` with timeout>0 → tight loop hammering `gh api` every iteration (sleepMilliseconds(0) returns immediately). Each iteration is an API call; 45s of continuous API calls. Minor; tunable foot-gun. Could clamp pollMs to a minimum (e.g. >=500ms). SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? Low risk; SUGGESTION.

3. **Token swap restore `if (swapped && sourceTok)`** — if `sourceToken` is absent but `silentToken` set, GH_TOKEN stays as App token after the belt; subsequent PAT operations in the same tick (update-branch, cancels) would run with the App token. This mirrors `stampValidationChecksForModule` exactly (parity), and jobParams on fa always carries sourceToken presumably. Parity with existing pattern → note as SUGGESTION (could read-back current GH_TOKEN before swap as the restore source).

4. **Belt PATCH without checking the PATCH result** — `gh api` failures throw? cli_execute_command presumably throws on nonzero exit; caught per check-run and warned; `concluded++` only on success. If PATCH fails (403), `concluded` undercounts and `result.cleaned` won't include the head → no clean marker → cure-side sweep remains backstop. Fail-soft, documented. OK.

5. **Marker regex `([0-9a-f]{7,40})`** — head sha 40-hex lowercase from GitHub — fine.

6. **`postGhostGuardAudit` reads ALL PR comments every tick a defer occurs** — until marker exists; after marker exists... wait: the audit still reads comments each tick (github_get_pr_comments) even when dedupe will suppress posting. Actually look: postGhostGuardAudit is called every tick with a defer present; it builds `wanted`, then reads comments, filters, finds nothing fresh → returns. So per tick with a persistently-queued run, one comment-list API call per tick. Modest. Could early-return if marks check... it must read comments to know. Fine.

8. **`concludeOrphanedCheckRuns` reads head check runs via PAT** (`github_get_commit_check_runs` bridge) — PAT-readable, per comment. OK.

Twin-guard intent (suppress parallel validation waste) — deferred cancels leave the duplicate running for minutes, not cancelled-instantly. 1. **Guard deferral + polling in tick loop** — blocking `waitForRunMaterialized` up to 45s per stale run inside `cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`, which runs inside `processRule`. With multiple stale runs, tick time extends significantly. Documented and accepted (PR notes). SUGGESTION at most.

2. **`waitForRunMaterialized` pollMs=0 edge** — `cancelMaterializePollMs: 0` with timeout>0 → tight loop hammering `gh api` every iteration (sleepMilliseconds(0) returns immediately). Each iteration is an API call; 45s of continuous API calls. Minor; tunable foot-gun. Could clamp pollMs to a minimum (e.g. >=500ms). SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? Low risk; SUGGESTION.

3. **Token swap restore `if (swapped && sourceTok)`** — if `sourceToken` is absent but `silentToken` set, GH_TOKEN stays as App token after the belt; subsequent PAT operations in the same tick (update-branch, cancels) would run with the App token. This mirrors `stampValidationChecksForModule` exactly (parity), and jobParams on fa always carries sourceToken presumably. Parity with existing pattern → note as SUGGESTION (could read-back current GH_TOKEN before swap as the restore source).

4. **Belt PATCH without checking the PATCH result** — `gh api` failures throw? cli_execute_command presumably throws on nonzero exit; caught per check-run and warned; `concluded++` only on success. If PATCH fails (403), `concluded` undercounts and `result.cleaned` won't include the head → no clean marker → cure-side sweep remains backstop. Fail-soft, documented. OK.

5. **Marker regex `([0-9a-f]{7,40})`** — head sha 40-hex lowercase from GitHub — fine.

6. **`postGhostGuardAudit` reads ALL PR comments every tick a defer occurs** — until marker exists; after marker exists... wait: the audit still reads comments each tick (github_get_pr_comments) even when dedupe will suppress posting. Actually look: postGhostGuardAudit is called every tick with a defer present; it builds `wanted`, then reads comments, filters, finds nothing fresh → returns. So per tick with a persistently-queued run, one comment-list API call per tick. Modest. Could early-return if marks check... it must read comments to know. Fine.

7. **Audit comment body**: contains both defer and clean lines plus explanation — fine.

8. **`concludeOrphanedCheckRuns` reads head check runs via PAT** (`github_get_commit_check_runs` bridge) — PAT-readable, per comment. OK.

9. **Backward compatibility of `cancelStaleDispatchedRuns` return type** — changed from array to object; both in-repo call sites updated. Any other consumer? grep showed only the two call sites. There is a doc comment at line 4138 referencing it (READ-ONLY note). OK.

10. **AC verification**:
- AC1: ghost #5 replay — defer on queued tested. Belt + guard cover "no orphaned in_progress check-run remains". Tested.
- AC2: 24h soak — live metric, not verifiable here.
- AC3: duplicates still suppressed — deferral means the duplicate run keeps occupying queue until materialized, then cancelled. Twin-guard intent (suppress parallel validation waste) — deferred cancels leave the duplicate running for minutes, not cancelled-instantly. AC3 says "duplicate dispatches are still suppressed, just safely" — eventual suppression. There's a subtle behavior consideration: during the defer window, two validation runs on different heads are active simultaneously — that's inherent. Tested multi-run sweep.
- AC4: live.

11. **One genuine design question**: In the validate_pr call site (line ~2226), `postGhostGuardAudit` is called BEFORE `dispatchCiWorkflow`. Good.

12. **`gh848Action` in tests uses `cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs: 25, cancelMaterializePollMs: 1`** — busy-wait loop of ~25ms; fine.

13. **The header docblock awkward line-break**: "0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.\n   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval." — a dangling "jobParams." sentence fragment. Cosmetic SUGGESTION.

14. **Belt only scans the cancelled run's head check-runs — but a check-run pending whose run link is unparseable** (`runIdOf` null) → not matched, skipped. Those are ghosts the belt can't attribute; cure-side sweep handles. Documented. OK.

15. **Security**: no injection — run ids and check-run ids are numeric from API. The PATCH command `-f conclusion=cancelled` fine. Secrets: silentToken swapped into GH_TOKEN env — established pattern; not logged. In the test, tokens are placeholders. No token logging in new code. OK.

16. **`result.cleaned` entries use `r.head_sha`** — the cancelled run's head sha; marker posted on the current PR (prNumber) — but wait: the cancelled run belongs to the same branch `ticket.branch`; its head_sha is an older head of the same PR. The marker is posted on the PR — fine since branch-scoped.

17. One more: in `cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`, `waitForRunMaterialized` runs BEFORE checking DRY? No — DRY returns earlier. Good.

18. **`postGhostGuardAudit` in DRY returns early** — and test asserts no marker in DRY for the gh-846 flow; but defer path in DRY? cancelStaleDispatchedRuns returns early empty in DRY so no defers. OK.

19. WaitForRunMaterialized probe: `mcpParse((res||{}).output || (res||{}).stdout || res)` — if res is a string, `(res||{}).output` is undefined, `...stdout` undefined, falls to `res` → mcpParse(string) → JSON.parse. Good. If cli_execute_command returns '' (like the test stub returns '' for unmatched), mcpParse('') → null → status null → defer. Good — the fail-defer contract also covers '' but '' doesn't throw. Actually mcpParse('') → !result → null. Good.

20. Test at line ~2205: added `actions/runs/111` stub returning in_progress — consistent.

Token restore parity: stampValidationChecksForModule has identical contract, so belt is consistent — SUGGESTION. pollMs=0: a tunable foot-gun, but defaults sane and it's an escape hatch — SUGGESTION.

Anything IMPORTANT? Consider: `cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs` default 45s blocking sleep inside the tick. On fa, ticks process many PR rules; if say 5 stale runs are queued, that's up to 3.75 min added serially. The tick may have a watchdog timeout. That's exactly what gh-846 wanted to cancel (dead-head run queued 50+ min ahead of useful mac queue work). Failures identical except the summary count line. No regressions.

Now, final review assessment. Let me enumerate findings:

**Analysis of the core logic:**

1. **Guard deferral + polling in tick loop** — blocking `waitForRunMaterialized` up to 45s per stale run inside `cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`, which runs inside `processRule`. With multiple stale runs, tick time extends significantly. Documented and accepted (PR notes). SUGGESTION at most.

2. **`waitForRunMaterialized` pollMs=0 edge** — `cancelMaterializePollMs: 0` with timeout>0 → tight loop hammering `gh api` every iteration (sleepMilliseconds(0) returns immediately). Each iteration is an API call; 45s of continuous API calls. Minor; tunable foot-gun. Could clamp pollMs to a minimum (e.g. >=500ms). SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? Low risk; SUGGESTION.

3. **Token swap restore `if (swapped && sourceTok)`** — if `sourceToken` is absent but `silentToken` set, GH_TOKEN stays as App token after the belt; subsequent PAT operations in the same tick (update-branch, cancels) would run with the App token. This mirrors `stampValidationChecksForModule` exactly (parity), and jobParams on fa always carries sourceToken presumably. Parity with existing pattern → note as SUGGESTION (could read-back current GH_TOKEN before swap as the restore source).

4. **Belt PATCH without checking the PATCH result** — `gh api` failures throw? cli_execute_command presumably throws on nonzero exit; caught per check-run and warned; `concluded++` only on success. If PATCH fails (403), `concluded` undercounts and `result.cleaned` won't include the head → no clean marker → cure-side sweep remains backstop. Fail-soft, documented. OK.

## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: The gh-848 ghost-guard (guard + belt + audit) is a well-scoped, well-tested fix for the queued-cancel orphan check-runs seizing the merge gate; it supersedes the gh-846 same-tick queued cancel safely and satisfies the ticket ACs as far as they are verifiable off-live (AC2/AC4 are soak/live metrics).

**Key Issues**: No blocking issues. Local node-harness run: all 9 new gh-848 tests pass; failure set is byte-identical to `main` (69 pre-existing harness mock gaps per `quality.yml`). Three suggestions: clamp `cancelMaterializePollMs` to a sane floor, snapshot `GH_TOKEN` before the App-token swap when `sourceToken` is absent, and fix a dangling `jobParams.` fragment in the header docblock.

**Next Steps**:
1. Merge as-is; the suggestions are non-blocking polish.
2. Track AC2 (ghost count = 0/day on fa) and AC4 (fa #1457-class merges without operator resets) during the live soak.

💡 **SUGGESTION: snapshot the ambient `GH_TOKEN` as the restore source when `sourceToken` is absent**

The restore contract `if (swapped && sourceTok)` means that when `jobParams.silentToken` is set but `sourceToken` is missing/empty, `GH_TOKEN` stays swapped to the GitHub App token after the belt finishes — every subsequent PAT operation in the same tick (update-branch dance, other `gh api` calls) would silently run with the App token instead of the PAT. This mirrors `stampValidationChecksForModule` exactly (established parity, so not blocking), but both sites share the fragility. Reading the current `GH_TOKEN` via `java.lang.System.getenv('GH_TOKEN')` (the bridge already exposes it in `node_testRunner`'s mock) before the swap, and restoring to that snapshot when `sourceToken` is falsy, closes the leak for both.

💡 **SUGGESTION: dangling `jobParams.` sentence fragment in the header docblock**

The docblock sentence breaks mid-reference:

```
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.
```

reads as "0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams." followed by an orphan paragraph. Merge into one sentence: `0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.`

Now, final review assessment. Let me enumerate findings:

**Analysis of the core logic:**

1. **Guard deferral + polling in tick loop** — blocking `waitForRunMaterialized` up to 45s per stale run inside `cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`, which runs inside `processRule`. With multiple stale runs, tick time extends significantly. Documented and accepted (PR notes). SUGGESTION at most.

2. **`waitForRunMaterialized` pollMs=0 edge** — `cancelMaterializePollMs: 0` with timeout>0 → tight loop hammering `gh api` every iteration (sleepMilliseconds(0) returns immediately). Each iteration is an API call; 45s of continuous API calls. Minor; tunable foot-gun. Could clamp pollMs to a minimum (e.g. >=500ms). SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? Low risk; SUGGESTION.

3. **Token swap restore `if (swapped && sourceTok)`** — if `sourceToken` is absent but `silentToken` set, GH_TOKEN stays as App token after the belt; subsequent PAT operations in the same tick (update-branch, cancels) would run with the App token. This mirrors `stampValidationChecksForModule` exactly (parity), and jobParams on fa always carries sourceToken presumably. Parity with existing pattern → note as SUGGESTION (could read-back current GH_TOKEN before swap as the restore source).

4. **Belt PATCH without checking the PATCH result** — `gh api` failures throw? cli_execute_command presumably throws on nonzero exit; caught per check-run and warned; `concluded++` only on success. If PATCH fails (403), `concluded` undercounts and `result.cleaned` won't include the head → no clean marker → cure-side sweep remains backstop. Fail-soft, documented. OK.

5. **Marker regex `([0-9a-f]{7,40})`** — head sha 40-hex lowercase from GitHub — fine.

6. **`postGhostGuardAudit` reads ALL PR comments every tick a defer occurs** — until marker exists; after marker exists... wait: the audit still reads comments each tick (github_get_pr_comments) even when dedupe will suppress posting. Actually look: postGhostGuardAudit is called every tick with a defer present; it builds `wanted`, then reads comments, filters, finds nothing fresh → returns. So per tick with a persistently-queued run, one comment-list API call per tick. Modest. Could early-return if marks check... it must read comments to know. Fine.

7. **Audit comment body**: contains both defer and clean lines plus explanation — fine.

8. **`concludeOrphanedCheckRuns` reads head check runs via PAT** (`github_get_commit_check_runs` bridge) — PAT-readable, per comment. OK.

9. **Backward compatibility of `cancelStaleDispatchedRuns` return type** — changed from array to object; both in-repo call sites updated. Any other consumer? grep showed only the two call sites. There is a doc comment at line 4138 referencing it (READ-ONLY note). OK.

10. **AC verification**:
- AC1: ghost #5 replay — defer on queued tested. Belt + guard cover "no orphaned in_progress check-run remains". Tested.
- AC2: 24h soak — live metric, not verifiable here.
- AC3: duplicates still suppressed — deferral means the duplicate run keeps occupying queue until materialized, then cancelled. Twin-guard intent (suppress parallel validation waste) — deferred cancels leave the duplicate running for minutes, not cancelled-instantly. AC3 says "duplicate dispatches are still suppressed, just safely" — eventual suppression. There's a subtle behavior consideration: during the defer window, two validation runs on different heads are active simultaneously — that's inherent. Tested multi-run sweep.
- AC4: live.

11. **One genuine design question**: In the validate_pr call site (line ~2226), `postGhostGuardAudit` is called BEFORE `dispatchCiWorkflow`. Good.

12. **`gh848Action` in tests uses `cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs: 25, cancelMaterializePollMs: 1`** — busy-wait loop of ~25ms; fine.

13. **The header docblock awkward line-break**: "0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.\n   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval." — a dangling "jobParams." sentence fragment. Cosmetic SUGGESTION.

14. **Belt only scans the cancelled run's head check-runs — but a check-run pending whose run link is unparseable** (`runIdOf` null) → not matched, skipped. Those are ghosts the belt can't attribute; cure-side sweep handles. Documented. OK.

15. **Security**: no injection — run ids and check-run ids are numeric from API. The PATCH command `-f conclusion=cancelled` fine. Secrets: silentToken swapped into GH_TOKEN env — established pattern; not logged. In the test, tokens are placeholders. No token logging in new code. OK.

16. **`result.cleaned` entries use `r.head_sha`** — the cancelled run's head sha; marker posted on the current PR (prNumber) — but wait: the cancelled run belongs to the same branch `ticket.branch`; its head_sha is an older head of the same PR. The marker is posted on the PR — fine since branch-scoped.

17. One more: in `cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`, `waitForRunMaterialized` runs BEFORE checking DRY? No — DRY returns earlier. Good.

18. **`postGhostGuardAudit` in DRY returns early** — and test asserts no marker in DRY for the gh-846 flow; but defer path in DRY? cancelStaleDispatchedRuns returns early empty in DRY so no defers. OK.

19. WaitForRunMaterialized probe: `mcpParse((res||{}).output || (res||{}).stdout || res)` — if res is a string, `(res||{}).output` is undefined, `...stdout` undefined, falls to `res` → mcpParse(string) → JSON.parse. Good. If cli_execute_command returns '' (like the test stub returns '' for unmatched), mcpParse('') → null → status null → defer. Good — the fail-defer contract also covers '' but '' doesn't throw. Actually mcpParse('') → !result → null. Good.

20. Test at line ~2205: added `actions/runs/111` stub returning in_progress — consistent.

So the verdict: no BLOCKING. Findings: a couple of SUGGESTIONs, maybe one IMPORTANT? Let me think about whether the pollMs=0 hammering or token-restore deserves IMPORTANT. Token restore parity: stampValidationChecksForModule has identical contract, so belt is consistent — SUGGESTION. pollMs=0: a tunable foot-gun, but defaults sane and it's an escape hatch — SUGGESTION.

Anything IMPORTANT? Consider: `cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs` default 45s blocking sleep inside the tick. On fa, ticks process many PR rules; if say 5 stale runs are queued, that's up to 3.75 min added serially. The tick may have a watchdog timeout. But this is a design trade-off documented and accepted in PR notes ("accepted by design"). I'll mention as SUGGESTION in general comment rather than inline.

Another possible IMPORTANT: the defer means a stale queued run may NEVER be cancelled if GitHub leaves it queued (e.g. runner starvation) — the run consumes a queue slot for potentially hours. That's exactly what gh-846 wanted to cancel (dead-head run queued 50+ min ahead of useful mac queue work). With defer, the ghost-window protection wins over queue-waste — accepted by design, documented in PR notes.

blocks.text:
Failures identical except the summary count line. No regressions.

Now, final review assessment. Let me enumerate findings:

**Analysis of the core logic:**

1. **Guard deferral + polling in tick loop** — blocking `waitForRunMaterialized` up to 45s per stale run inside `cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`, which runs inside `processRule`. With multiple stale runs, tick time extends significantly. Documented and accepted (PR notes). SUGGESTION at most.

2. **`waitForRunMaterialized` pollMs=0 edge** — `cancelMaterializePollMs: 0` with timeout>0 → tight loop hammering `gh api` every iteration (sleepMilliseconds(0) returns immediately). Each iteration is an API call; 45s of continuous API calls. Minor; tunable foot-gun. Could clamp pollMs to a minimum (e.g. >=500ms). SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? Low risk; SUGGESTION.

3. **Token swap restore `if (swapped && sourceTok)`** — if `sourceToken` is absent but `silentToken` set, GH_TOKEN stays as App token after the belt; subsequent PAT operations in the same tick (update-branch, cancels) would run with the App token. This mirrors `stampValidationChecksForModule` exactly (parity), and jobParams on fa always carries sourceToken presumably. Parity with existing pattern → note as SUGGESTION (could read-back current GH_TOKEN before swap as the restore source).

4. **Belt PATCH without checking the PATCH result** — `gh api` failures throw? cli_execute_command presumably throws on nonzero exit; caught per check-run and warned; `concluded++` only on success. If PATCH fails (403), `concluded` undercounts and `result.cleaned` won't include the head → no clean marker → cure-side sweep remains backstop. Fail-soft, documented. OK.

5. **Marker regex `([0-9a-f]{7,40})`** — head sha 40-hex lowercase from GitHub — fine.

6. **`postGhostGuardAudit` reads ALL PR comments every tick a defer occurs** — until marker exists; after marker exists... wait: the audit still reads comments each tick (github_get_pr_comments) even when dedupe will suppress posting. Actually look: postGhostGuardAudit is called every tick with a defer present; it builds `wanted`, then reads comments, filters, finds nothing fresh → returns. So per tick with a persistently-queued run, one comment-list API call per tick. Modest. Could early-return if marks check... it must read comments to know. Fine.

7. **Audit comment body**: contains both defer and clean lines plus explanation — fine.

8. **`concludeOrphanedCheckRuns` reads head check runs via PAT** (`github_get_commit_check_runs` bridge) — PAT-readable, per comment. OK.

9. **Backward compatibility of `cancelStaleDispatchedRuns` return type** — changed from array to object; both in-repo call sites updated. Any other consumer? grep showed only the two call sites. There is a doc comment at line 4138 referencing it (READ-ONLY note). OK.

10. **AC verification**:
- AC1: ghost #5 replay — defer on queued tested. Belt + guard cover "no orphaned in_progress check-run remains". Tested.
- AC2: 24h soak — live metric, not verifiable here.
- AC3: duplicates still suppressed — deferral means the duplicate run keeps occupying queue until materialized, then cancelled. Twin-guard intent (suppress parallel validation waste) — deferred cancels leave the duplicate running for minutes, not cancelled-instantly. AC3 says "duplicate dispatches are still suppressed, just safely" — eventual suppression. There's a subtle behavior consideration: during the defer window, two validation runs on different heads are active simultaneously — that's inherent. Tested multi-run sweep.
- AC4: live.

11. **One genuine design question**: In the validate_pr call site (line ~2226), `postGhostGuardAudit` is called BEFORE `dispatchCiWorkflow`. Good.

12. **`gh848Action` in tests uses `cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs: 25, cancelMaterializePollMs: 1`** — busy-wait loop of ~25ms; fine.

13. **The header docblock awkward line-break**: "0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.\n   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval." — a dangling "jobParams." sentence fragment. Cosmetic SUGGESTION.

14. **Belt only scans the cancelled run's head check-runs — but a check-run pending whose run link is unparseable** (`runIdOf` null) → not matched, skipped. Those are ghosts the belt can't attribute; cure-side sweep handles. Documented. OK.

15. **Security**: no injection — run ids and check-run ids are numeric from API. The PATCH command `-f conclusion=cancelled` fine. Secrets: silentToken swapped into GH_TOKEN env — established pattern; not logged. In the test, tokens are placeholders. No token logging in new code. OK.

16. **`result.cleaned` entries use `r.head_sha`** — the cancelled run's head sha; marker posted on the current PR (prNumber) — but wait: the cancelled run belongs to the same branch `ticket.branch`; its head_sha is an older head of the same PR. The marker is posted on the PR — fine since branch-scoped.

17. One more: in `cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`, `waitForRunMaterialized` runs BEFORE checking DRY? No — DRY returns earlier. Good.

18. **`postGhostGuardAudit` in DRY returns early** — and test asserts no marker in DRY for the gh-846 flow; but defer path in DRY? cancelStaleDispatchedRuns returns early empty in DRY so no defers. OK.

19. WaitForRunMaterialized probe: `mcpParse((res||{}).output || (res||{}).stdout || res)` — if res is a string, `(res||{}).output` is undefined, `...stdout` undefined, falls to `res` → mcpParse(string) → JSON.parse. Good. If cli_execute_command returns '' (like the test stub returns '' for unmatched), mcpParse('') → null → status null → defer. Good — the fail-defer contract also covers '' but '' doesn't throw. Actually mcpParse('') → !result → null. Good.

20. Test at line ~2205: added `actions/runs/111` stub returning in_progress — consistent.

So the verdict: no BLOCKING. Findings: a couple of SUGGESTIONs, maybe one IMPORTANT? Let me think about whether the pollMs=0 hammering or token-restore deserves IMPORTANT. Token restore parity: stampValidationChecksForModule has identical contract, so belt is consistent — SUGGESTION. pollMs=0: a tunable foot-gun, but defaults sane and it's an escape hatch — SUGGESTION.

Anything IMPORTANT? Consider: `cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs` default 45s blocking sleep inside the tick. On fa, ticks process many PR rules; if say 5 stale runs are queued, that's up to 3.75 min added serially. The tick may have a watchdog timeout. But this is a design trade-off documented and accepted in PR notes ("accepted by design"). I'll mention as SUGGESTION in general comment rather than inline.

Another possible IMPORTANT: the defer means a stale queued run may NEVER be cancelled if GitHub leaves it queued (e.g. runner starvation) — the run consumes a queue slot for potentially hours. That's exactly what gh-846 wanted to cancel (dead-head run queued 50+ min ahead of useful mac queue work). With defer, the ghost-window protection wins over queue-waste — accepted by design, documented in PR notes.

One more check — `postGhostGuardAudit` duplicates: within one call, `seen` dedupes. Across defer+clean for same head, both lines posted in one comment. Fine.

Check the regex issue: marker timestamp `(\S+)` — ISO from toISOString. Date.parse handles. OK.

Also verify the "belt" runs after cancel with `|| true` cancel command — cancel command has `|| true`, so a failed cancel (e.g., 409 already completed) still counts as "cancelled.push(r)" and belt runs. Pre-existing semantics (cancel || true then push). Fine.

Failures identical except the summary count line. No regressions.

Now, final review assessment. Let me enumerate findings:

**Analysis of the core logic:**

1. **Guard deferral + polling in tick loop** — blocking `waitForRunMaterialized` up to 45s per stale run inside `cancelStaleDispatchedRuns`, which runs inside `processRule`. With multiple stale runs, tick time extends significantly. Documented and accepted (PR notes). SUGGESTION at most.

2. **`waitForRunMaterialized` pollMs=0 edge** — `cancelMaterializePollMs: 0` with timeout>0 → tight loop hammering `gh api` every iteration (sleepMilliseconds(0) returns immediately). Each iteration is an API call; 45s of continuous API calls. Minor; tunable foot-gun. Could clamp pollMs to a minimum (e.g. >=500ms). SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? Low risk; SUGGESTION.

3. **Token swap restore `if (swapped && sourceTok)`** — if `sourceToken` is absent but `silentToken` set, GH_TOKEN stays as App token after the belt; subsequent PAT operations in the same tick (update-branch, cancels) would run with the App token.
